summary: Implemented DefaultRuntimeIdentifierProvider using RuntimeInformation. Returns one of 5 canonical RIDs or throws PlatformNotSupportedException. 3 new tests pass on Windows x64 CI host without skipping; 37 total tests pass.

comments.note: CachedRid is a static field computed once at class load. This is correct for immutable process-level state, but makes the 'unsupported platform' path untestable without reflection or subclassing. If testability of that path becomes important, consider making ResolveRid() internal/virtual or injecting a platform-check delegate.
No observations — code in the touched files is clean and consistent.

summary: Build clean. All 3 DefaultRuntimeIdentifierProviderTests pass on Windows x64 without skipping. 42/42 VideoIndexer.Tests pass. All 3 acceptance criteria verified.

metrics.test_coverage: 3 tests: non-null on supported host, one-of-5-RIDs check, exact win-x64 value on Windows x64

comments.note: PlatformNotSupportedException path (CachedRid == null) is untestable without reflection due to the static field computed at class load time. Low risk since the static approach is correct for immutable process-level state.

Tests use early-return (not xUnit Skip) on unsupported hosts. They 'pass' without asserting on those platforms. This is a pragmatic cross-platform design but means a misconfigured provider on a non-standard host would silently pass.

summary: Code review passed. DefaultRuntimeIdentifierProvider is clean, idiomatic, and well-documented. Static caching is correctly reasoned. Exception message is diagnostic. Interface-to-implementation boundary is sound. No blocking issues found. One low-priority DRY observation in tests and one documentation-forward item recorded.

comments.note: The `isSupported` guard predicate is duplicated verbatim across GetRuntimeIdentifier_OnSupportedHost_ReturnsNonNullString and GetRuntimeIdentifier_OnSupportedHost_ReturnsKnownRid. A private static IsOnSupportedHost() helper in the test class would eliminate the repetition without changing behavior.

[documentation-forward] IRuntimeIdentifierProvider.GetRuntimeIdentifier() interface contract is missing an <exception cref='PlatformNotSupportedException'> tag. The PlatformNotSupportedException behavior is only documented on the implementation class via <inheritdoc />. Adding the <exception> tag to the interface makes the contract discoverable to consumers without needing to inspect the concrete class.
